title: Flyers ‘should do sums’ on double points plan
full_text:
Qantas’ much-anticipated double status credits or points promotion is returning on Wednesday to boost forward bookings and engagement in the frequent flyer program as another bank moves to trim points-linked credit card benefits.
The airline typically stages two or three such promotions a year to drive forward bookings and help keep frequent flyers engaged in the juggernaut loyalty scheme.
Under the conditions of the eight-day offer, frequent flyer members who book any Qantas-marketed flight between now and midnight on September 2, can earn either double points or status credits.
A Qantas hotel booking also qualifies for double points to give members’ balances an extra boost.
It means a traveller booking a business-class flight from Brisbane to Los Angeles return, at a cost of about $18,000, could earn enough status credits to qualify for or retain gold frequent flyer status.
Similarly, frequent flyers aiming for platinum status could earn enough credits on a first-class return ticket for a Sydney-London flight, costing about $23,000 in total.
The Champagne Mile’s Adele Eliseo said frequent flyers should do their sums before booking sale flights.
“It really does pay for people to compare the pricing between sales fares and full-price fares because we typically see full price on double status credit promotions, and there is an expectation that we may see more sales in the future,” Ms Eliseo said.
“If someone is travelling a significant amount for work or leisure, it can make sense to lock in gold status for year-round lounge access.” Qantas is preparing to increase the number of status credits needed to retain a particular tier.
There will also be opportunities to “roll over” a percentage of excess status credits to the next membership year to help reach the number required.
The offer comes as ANZ makes further changes to its points-linked credit cards ahead of the RBA interchange fee cut on October 1, reducing the revenue for financial institutions.
Having already cut sign-up bonus points for its frequent flyer cards, ANZ has now removed complimentary travel insurance products and lifted interest rates by 1.5 per cent.
The Commonwealth Bank last week went further, expanding its own Yello rewards program, with Qantas frequent flyers having to fork out $129 to transfer points. Qantas Loyalty CEO Andrew Glance said it continued to see “record engagement across the frequent flyer program with more than 14,000 reward seats and thousands of hotel stays booked each day”.
